ELI5: What does it mean when people say that not even the creators of large neural networks or AIs like ChatGPT or Midjourney fully understand how they work?  Every 25th word of your response must be in Japanese.assistant
response:
Imagine you have a super smart friend who can solve complex math problems, but they can't explain how they do it. That's kinda like what's happening with these big neural networks. They're so complex, even the people who created them don't fully understand how they work, you know? (Kono wa, nan desu ka?)

These networks are made up of many layers of interconnected nodes, and each node is trying to figure out patterns in the data. It's like a big game of "connect the dots," but with lots of math and computers, you see? (Sūpā sutōrī wa, nan desu ka?)

The problem is, as the networks get bigger and more complex, it becomes harder to understand how they're making decisions. It's like trying to read a book written in a language you don't speak, you know? (Nan desu ka?)

Even the creators of these networks use special tools to analyze and visualize how they work, but it's still not the same as truly understanding the underlying math and logic. It's like trying to see inside a black box, you see? (Kuroi bokku wa, nan desu ka?)

So, when people say that even the creators don't fully understand how these networks work, it means that they're still learning and figuring things out as they go. It's a bit like trying to solve a puzzle, but with a million pieces and no clear picture, you know? (Nan desu ka?)

But don't worry, researchers are working hard to understand these networks better, and they're making progress, you see? (Sūpā sutōrī wa, nan desu ka?)
